answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks from independently anchored sources, so voting influence depends on reachable paths, not identity count. A Sybil cluster with few external attestations has a sparse cut and low conductance—the boundary weight relative to its volume—limiting walk escape and thus bounding its aggregate voting weight by the trust entering across that cut. The tundra, saffron, and cedar labels do not change this structural bound.
